thm:generalMonicCount.statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:generalMonicCount} For every $\varepsilon>0$, as $H\to\infty$, the number of monic integral cubic polynomials with Galois group $C_3$ and root height at most $H$ is \[ H^3P(\log H)+O_\varepsilon(H^{2+\varepsilon}), \] where \begin{equation} P(X)=\frac{220\alpha}{243} \biggl(X+\mu-\frac{\zeta'(2)}{\zeta(2)}+ \beta +\log2-\frac{5}{88}\log3 +\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{10}-\frac{17}{15}\biggr) -\frac{20\pi\sqrt3}{81}. \end{equation} \end{theorem}

thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount.statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount} For every $\varepsilon>0$, as $H\to\infty$, the number of monic integral trace-one cubic polynomials with Galois group $C_3$ and root height at most $H$ is \[ H^2P_1(\log H)+O_\varepsilon(H^{1+\varepsilon}) \] where \begin{equation} P_1(X)=\frac\alpha3 \biggl(X+\mu-\frac{\zeta'(2)}{\zeta(2)} + \beta +\frac78\log3-\frac12\biggr) -\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt3}. \end{equation} \end{theorem}

thm:exactFormula.statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:exactFormula} For $m\geq1$ let $a_E(m)$ denote the number of ideals of norm $m$ in the ring of integers $\mcO_E$ of $E$. If $t^3-t^2+at+b\in\ZZ[t]$ has Galois group $C_3$, then $a\leq0$. Fix $a \in \ZZ_{\leq 0}$ and put $n=1-3a$. The number of polynomials of the form $t^3 -t^2 + at + b \in \ZZ[t]$ with Galois group $C_3$ is equal to \begin{equation} \tfrac{1}{2}\big(a_E(n^3)-a_E(n)\big). \end{equation} \end{theorem}

thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula.statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula} For $\mathrm{Re}(s)>2$ the series below converges absolutely, and \begin{equation} \sum_{P \in (\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ)} H(P)^{-s} = \left(1-\frac{1}{3^{s/2}}\right)^2 \xi\left(\frac s2\right)^2 \prod_{q\equiv2\pmod{3}}\left(1-\frac{1}{q^{s}}\right) \prod_{p\equiv1\pmod{3}}\left(1-\frac{3}{p^{s}}+\frac{2}{p^{3s/2}}\right) \end{equation} where $\xi$ is the Dedekind zeta function of $E$. This height zeta function can be meromorphically continued to the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>1$ and its only pole in this region is at $s = 2$ with order $2$. \end{theorem}

cor:integralPointCount.statement: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:integralPointCount} For every $\varepsilon>0$, as $H\to\infty$, \[ \#\{P\in(\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ):H(P)\leq H\} =H^2Q(\log H)+O_\varepsilon(H^{1+\varepsilon}), \] where \begin{equation} Q(X)=\frac{2\alpha}{9} \biggl(X+\mu-\frac{\zeta'(2)}{\zeta(2)} +\beta+\frac38\log3-\frac12\biggr). \end{equation} \end{corollary}

thm:modularInterpretation.statement: \begin{theorem}[{\cite[\S2]{odesky2023moduli}}]\label{thm:modularInterpretation} The homogeneous variety $T$ is the moduli space for $C_3$-algebras with a given trace-one normal element. In particular, there is a bijection between rational points of $T$ and equivalence classes of $C_3$-algebras $K/\mathbb Q$ equipped with a trace one normal element $x \in K$. \end{theorem}

example:twoRationalPointsSamePoly.statement: \begin{example}\label{example:twoRationalPointsSamePoly} Let $K$ be a cubic abelian number field. Then $K$, equipped with its canonical Galois action, is a $C_3$-algebra. The twist $K'$ of the $C_3$-algebra $K$ by the outer automorphism $g \mapsto g^{-1}$ of $C_3$ (with twisted action $g \ast x = g^{-1}x$) is not isomorphic to $K$ as a $C_3$-algebra.\footnote{ In terms of Galois cohomology, the non-cohomologous $1$-cocycles in $H^1(\QQ,C_3)$ corresponding to the $C_3$-algebras $K$ and $K'$ have the same image under the canonical map $H^1(\QQ,C_3) \to H^1(\QQ,S_3)$ because the outer automorphism of $C_3$ is realized by $S_3$-conjugation.} \end{example}

example:splitAlgebra.statement: \begin{example}\label{example:splitAlgebra} Let $K_{\text{spl}} = \QQ^3$, the split cubic algebra. Then $C_3\subset S_3 = \mathrm{Aut}_{\text{$\QQ$-alg}}(K_{\text{spl}})$ and $K_{\text{spl}}$, equipped with its canonical $C_3$-action, is a $C_3$-algebra. Any transposition gives an isomorphism of $C_3$-algebras from $K_{\text{spl}}$ to its twist $K_{\text{spl}}'$. \end{example}

example:splitAlgebraNormalElement.statement: \begin{example}\label{example:splitAlgebraNormalElement} An element $x$ of trace one in the split $C_3$-algebra $K_{\text{spl}}$ is normal if and only if $x$ either has distinct coordinates or exactly two identical coordinates. For such a normal element $x$, the pairs $(K_{\text{spl}},x)$ and $(K_{\text{spl}}',x)$ are equivalent if and only if $x$ has exactly two identical coordinates (swapping the identical coordinates gives the required isomorphism); in particular, if $x$ has distinct coordinates then $(K_{\text{spl}},x)$ and $(K_{\text{spl}}',x)$ determine different rational points of $\mathcal G_1/C_3$, even though $K_{\text{spl}}$ and $K_{\text{spl}}'$ are isomorphic as $C_3$-algebras. \end{example}

prop:basicfacts.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:basicfacts} Let $w$ be a place of $E$ lying over a place $v$ of $\QQ$. There is an exact sequence \begin{equation} 1 \longrightarrow K_v^{\mathrm{max}} \longrightarrow T(\QQ_v) \xlongrightarrow{\ell_w} \mathfrak t_w. \end{equation} If $w$ is infinite then $\ell_w$ is surjective, and if $w$ is finite then the image of $\ell_w$ is the lattice $X_\ast(T_{E})^{\Gamma(w/v)}$. \end{proposition}

lemma:heightformula.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:heightformula} Let $\mathbf 1$ denote the global section in $H^0(S_E,\mathcal O(3D_0))$ associated to the effective Cartier divisor $3D_0$, namely the image of $1$ under the natural inclusion $\mathcal O_{S_E}\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_{S_E}(3D_0)$. The space $H^0(S_E,\mathcal O(3D_0))$ is spanned over $E$ by the following four weight vectors: \begin{align}\label{eqn:weightVectors} &\mathbf 1,\qquad (1-3e_2e_1^{-2})\mathbf 1, \\ &(e_1^3-\tfrac 92 e_1 e_2+ \tfrac{27}{2} e_3 + \tfrac{\sqrt{-27}}{2} \sqrt{\mathrm{disc}}) e_1^{-3}\mathbf 1,\qquad (e_1^3-\tfrac 92 e_1 e_2+ \tfrac{27}{2} e_3 - \tfrac{\sqrt{-27}}{2} \sqrt{\mathrm{disc}}) e_1^{-3}\mathbf 1 \end{align} where $\sqrt{\mathrm{disc}} \coloneq (X-Z)(Y-X)(Z-Y)$. The associated characters of $T_E$ are, respectively, \begin{equation} 1,\quad \chi^{a'+b'},\quad \chi^{2a'+b'},\quad\chi^{2b'+a'} \end{equation} where $a' = 2v_1^\vee - v_2^\vee$ and $b' = 2v_2^\vee - v_1^\vee$ in the character lattice $M_E = X^\ast T_E$ and $(v_1^\vee,v_2^\vee)$ is the dual basis to $(v_1,v_2)$. \end{lemma}

eqn:weightVectors.statement: \begin{align}\label{eqn:weightVectors} &\mathbf 1,\qquad (1-3e_2e_1^{-2})\mathbf 1, \\ &(e_1^3-\tfrac 92 e_1 e_2+ \tfrac{27}{2} e_3 + \tfrac{\sqrt{-27}}{2} \sqrt{\mathrm{disc}}) e_1^{-3}\mathbf 1,\qquad (e_1^3-\tfrac 92 e_1 e_2+ \tfrac{27}{2} e_3 - \tfrac{\sqrt{-27}}{2} \sqrt{\mathrm{disc}}) e_1^{-3}\mathbf 1 \end{align}

lemma:affineIntegrality.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:affineIntegrality} Write $e_2,e_3,\delta$ for the dehomogenized invariants \[ e_2=\frac{XY+YZ+ZX}{\varepsilon^2},\qquad e_3=\frac{XYZ}{\varepsilon^3},\qquad \delta=\frac{X^2Y+Y^2Z+Z^2X}{\varepsilon^3}. \] Then \begin{equation}\label{eqn:affineC3invariants} \ZZ[X/\varepsilon,Y/\varepsilon]^{C_3} =\ZZ[e_2,e_3,\delta]. \end{equation} A rational point $P$ of $S\setminus D_0$ is integral if and only if $e_2(P),e_3(P)\in\ZZ$. \end{lemma}

prop:canonicalHeight.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:canonicalHeight} The characteristic polynomial $f = t^3-t^2+at+b \in \QQ[t]$ of a rational point $(K/\mathbb Q,x) \in T(\mathbb Q)$ has integer coefficients if and only if $(K/\mathbb Q,x)$ is integral. For any integral rational point $(K/\QQ,x)$ on $T$, \begin{equation} H((K/\mathbb Q,x),\mathcal O(D_0)) = \sqrt{1-3a}. \end{equation} \end{proposition}

lemma:rootVsToric.statement: \begin{lemma}[Root height and toric height]\label{lemma:rootVsToric} Let $P=(K/\QQ,x)$ be an integral rational point of $T$ with characteristic polynomial $f=t^3-t^2+at+b\in\ZZ[t]$. Write $H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)=H(P,\mathcal O(D_0))$ for its toric height and set $h(f)=\max(|a|^{1/2},|b|^{1/3})$, so that $H(f)=\max\{1,h(f)\}$. Then $a\leq0$ and $h(f)^2=-a, H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)^2=1+3h(f)^2$ so for every $B\geq0$, \begin{equation} h(f)\leq B \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)\leq\sqrt{1+3B^2}. \end{equation} In particular, $H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)\asymp H(f)$. The only polynomial here with $h(f)=0$ is $t^3-t^2$, for which $H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)=1$. \end{lemma}

prop:cyclotomicParametrization.statement: \begin{proposition}[Parametrization of monic abelian cubic trace-one polynomials by $\QQ(\sqrt{-3})^\times$]\label{prop:cyclotomicParametrization} The tori $T$ and $\mathcal G_1 = R^E_\QQ \mathcal \GG_m$ are isomorphic as algebraic groups over $\QQ$. Every rational point $(K/\QQ,x)$ of $T$ thereby determines an element of $\QQ(\sqrt{-3})^\times$ which is canonically determined up to the action of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal G_1)$. For integral rational points of $T$, the toric height $H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)\coloneqq\sqrt{1-3a}$ is identified with the square-root of the norm on $\QQ(\sqrt{-3})^\times$. Let $\zeta$ be a primitive cube root of unity. If $u+v\zeta \in \QQ(\sqrt{-3})^\times$ has norm $N$ and trace $T$, then the characteristic polynomial of the corresponding rational point $(K/\QQ,x)$ is \begin{equation} f=t^3-t^2+\tfrac{1}{3}(1 - N)t+\tfrac{1}{27}(N(3-T)-1) \in \QQ[t]. \end{equation} Such a polynomial either has Galois group $C_3$ or splits into three linear factors over $\QQ$, with at most two linear factors being the same. Conversely, a monic trace-one polynomial $f=t^3-t^2+at+b \in \QQ[t]$ which either has Galois group $C_3$ or splits into three linear factors over $\QQ$, with at most two linear factors being the same, can be expressed in this way for precisely two rational points of $T$ if $f$ has no repeated roots, or for precisely one rational point of $T$ if $f$ has a double root which is not a triple root. The elements $u+v\zeta \in \QQ(\sqrt{-3})^\times$ corresponding to $f=t^3-t^2+at+b$ will be the roots of the quadratic polynomial \begin{equation} g = t^2 - \left(3-\frac{1+27b}{1-3a}\right)t + 1-3a \in \QQ[t]. \end{equation} The polynomial $f$ will have integral coefficients if and only if \begin{equation}\label{eqn:integralityConditionsUsingCyclo} \begin{cases} u^2+v^2-uv \in 1+3 \ZZ \text{ and }\\ (u^2+v^2-uv)(3-2u+v) \in 1+27 \ZZ. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{proposition}

thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula2.statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula2} Fix any $s \in (\CC^{\Sigma(1)})^{\Gamma}$ with $\mathrm{Re}(s_0+s_1+s_2) > 2$. Then the multivariate Dirichlet series \begin{equation} Z(s)= \sum_{\substack{P \in T(\mathbb Q)\\\text{\emph{integral}}}} H(P,s)^{-1} \end{equation} is absolutely convergent and equals \begin{align} \left({1-3^{-z}}\right) \zeta(z) \prod_{q\equiv2\pmod{3}} \bparen{1+\frac{1}{q^{z}}}^{-1} \prod_{p\equiv1\pmod{3}} \bparen{1+\frac{3}{p^z}\bparen{1-\frac{1}{p^z}}^{-1}} \end{align} where $z = \frac{1}{2}(s_0+s_1+s_2)$. This multivariate Dirichlet series admits a meromorphic continuation to $\{s \in (\CC^{\Sigma(1)})^{\Gamma} : \mathrm{Re}(s_0+s_1+s_2) > 1\}$. \end{theorem}

prop:localIntegrality.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:localIntegrality} Let $v$ be a finite place of $\QQ$ and let $w$ be a place of $E$ lying over $v$. \begin{enumerate} \item If $v \neq 3$, then $1_v^{D_0}(x) = 1$ if and only if $\ell_w(x) \in \mathbb R_{\geq 0}v_1+\mathbb R_{\geq 0}v_2$. In particular $K_v^{D_0}=K_v^{\mathrm{max}}$. \item Let $v = 3$, let $w$ be the unique place of $E$ over $3$, and let $\mathfrak w = (1-\zeta)O_{E,w}$ be the maximal ideal of $O_{E,w}$, so that $3O_{E,w} = \mathfrak w^2$. The support of $1_3^{D_0}$ is the subgroup \begin{equation} K_{3,2}\coloneqq\iota^{-1}(1+\mathfrak w^2) =\iota^{-1}(1+3O_{E,w})\subset K_3^{\mathrm{max}}. \end{equation} \item Let $K^{\mathrm{max}}=\prod_v K_v^{\mathrm{max}}$ and $K^{D_0}=\prod_v K_v^{D_0}\subset K^{\mathrm{max}}$. The latter is the subgroup which fixes the characteristic function $1^{D_0}=\otimes_v1_v^{D_0}$ for integral points in $T(\AA)$, with $1_\infty^{D_0}=1$. Then \[ K_3^{D_0}=K_{3,2},\qquad K^{D_0}=K_{3,2}\times\prod_{v\neq3}K_v^{\mathrm{max}}. \] \end{enumerate} \end{proposition}

target.authorized_by_user: Authorized literature input; retained as an explicit hypothesis. See ../CORRESPONDENCE.md.

prop:heightFourierTransform.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:heightFourierTransform} Let $s \in (\CC^{\Sigma(1)})^{\Gamma}$ and assume $\mathrm{Re}(s_e)>0$ for each $e \in\{0,1,2\}$. Let $w$ be the infinite place of $E$. Let $\chi\in T(\RR)^\vee$ be a unitary character. If $\chi$ is ramified then $\widehat{H_\infty}(\chi,-s,D_0)$ is identically zero. If $\chi$ is unramified, then $\chi(x)= e(\langle \ell_w(x) ,m\rangle)$ for all $x \in T(\RR)$ for a unique $m \in \mathfrak t^\vee$, and \begin{equation}\label{eqn:infiniteHeightFourierTransform} \widehat{H_\infty}(\chi,-s,D_0) = \left(\frac{-1}{2\pi i}\right) \frac{s_0+s_1+s_2}{2\pi i} \frac{1}{(m(v_0)+\frac{s_0}{2\pi i})(m(v_0)-\frac{s_1+s_2}{2\pi i})}. \end{equation} Next let $v$ be a finite place of $\QQ$. For any unitary character $\chi\in T(\QQ_v)^\vee$, the integral defining $\widehat{H_v}(\chi,-s,D_0)$ converges absolutely to a holomorphic function of $s$ in the region $$\{s \in (\CC^{\Sigma(1)})^\Gamma : \mathrm{Re}(s_1),\mathrm{Re}(s_2)>0 \}.$$ Assume $v \neq 3$. Let $w$ be any place of $E$ lying over $v$. The local characteristic function $1_v^{D_0}$ is $K_v^{\mathrm{max}}$-invariant. If $\chi$ is ramified, then $\widehat{H_v}(\chi,-s,D_0)$ is identically zero. If $\chi$ is unramified then we may regard $\chi$ as a character on $X_\ast(T_{E})^{\Gamma(w/v)}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:basicfacts}) and \begin{equation}\label{eqn:finiteHeightFourierTransform} \widehat{H_v}(\chi,-s,D_0) = \sum_{\substack{n \in X_\ast(T_{E})^{\Gamma(w/v)}\\ n \in \mathbb R_{\geq 0}v_1+\mathbb R_{\geq 0}v_2} } \chi(n)^{-1} q_v^{\varphi(n)} . \end{equation} If $v = 3$ then the support of $x \mapsto H_3(x,-s,D_0)$ is the congruence subgroup $K_{3,2}$ of $K_3^{\mathrm{max}}$ of index six. Under the isomorphism $\iota:T(\QQ_3)\to E_w^\times$ the support corresponds to the subgroup $1+3O_{E,w}$ of $O_{E,w}^\times$ where $w$ is the unique place of $E$ lying over $3$. \end{proposition}

eqn:localfourierassumovern.statement: \begin{equation}\label{eqn:localfourierassumovern} \int_{T(\QQ_v)} H_v(x,s)^{-1}1_v^{D_0}(x)\chi(x)^{-1}\,d^\times x_v =\sum_{n \in N_w} q_v^{\frac{1}{e_v}\varphi(n)} 1_v^{D_0}(n) \chi(n)^{-1} = \sum_{\substack{n \in X_\ast(T_{E})^{\Gamma(w/v)}\\ n \in \mathbb R_{\geq 0}v_1+\mathbb R_{\geq 0}v_2} } \chi(n)^{-1} q_v^{\varphi(n)} . \end{equation}

prop:Lmap.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:Lmap} There is an exact sequence \begin{equation} 1 \longrightarrow K^{\mathrm{max}}/\mu^{\mathrm{max}} \longrightarrow T(\mathbb Q)\backslash T(\AA) \xlongrightarrow{\ell} \mathfrak t \longrightarrow 0 \end{equation} where $K^{\mathrm{max}}$ is the maximal compact subgroup of $T(\AA)$ and $\mu^{\mathrm{max}} = T(\QQ) \cap K^{\mathrm{max}}$. \end{proposition}

lemma:KprimeGroup.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:KprimeGroup} Let $K^{D_0}=K_{3,2}\times\prod_{v\neq3}K_v^{\mathrm{max}}$ be the subgroup of $K^{\mathrm{max}}$ fixing $1^{D_0}$, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:localIntegrality}. The map $\ell$ induces an isomorphism \begin{equation} T(\QQ)\backslash T(\AA)/K^{D_0} \xlongrightarrow{\sim} \mathfrak t. \end{equation} Let $a(u)\in T(\AA)$ have infinite component $\iota^{-1}(e^u)$ and all finite components one, so $\ell(a(u))=uv_0$. In this coordinate, the pushforward of the quotient measure is $du/6$. \end{lemma}

lemma:finiteFourierProduct.statement: \begin{lemma}[{Finite Fourier product}]\label{lemma:finiteFourierProduct} For $\operatorname{Re}(\sigma)>1$ and $t\in\RR$, put $\lambda=\sigma-\pi it$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eqn:finiteSpectralProduct} \widehat{H_{\mathrm{fin}}}(\chi_m,-s,D_0) =\frac16 \prod_{q\equiv2\pmod3}(1-q^{-2\lambda})^{-1} \prod_{p\equiv1\pmod3} \frac{1+2p^{-\lambda}}{(1-p^{-\lambda})^2} \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\label{eqn:finiteEulerBound} \left|\widehat{H_{\mathrm{fin}}}(\chi_m,-s,D_0)\right| \leq\widehat{H_{\mathrm{fin}}}(\chi_0,{-\operatorname{Re}(s)},D_0)<\infty. \end{equation} Here $\chi_0$ is the trivial character, corresponding to $m=0$. The Euler product converges absolutely and locally uniformly for $\operatorname{Re}(\lambda)>1$ and is bounded on every half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(\lambda)\geq\tau>1$. \end{lemma}

lemma:heightZetaConvergence.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:heightZetaConvergence} Let $s=(s_0,\sigma,\sigma)\in(\CC^{\Sigma(1)})^\Gamma$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s_0)>0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(\sigma)>1$, and put $f=H(\cdot,-s,D_0)$. Then $f\in L^1(T(\AA))$ and $\widehat f\,|_{T(\QQ)^\perp}\in L^1(T(\QQ)^\perp)$. \end{lemma}

lemma:poissonIntegral.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:poissonIntegral} For $s$ as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:heightZetaConvergence}, we have \begin{equation}\label{eqn:poissonEulerIntegral} Z(s)=6\int_\RR \widehat{H_\infty}(\chi_{m,\infty},-s,D_0) \widehat{H_{\mathrm{fin}}}(\chi_m,-s,D_0)\,dt, \end{equation} where both the series defining $Z(s)$ and the integral converge absolutely. \end{lemma}

lemma:simplifiedZ(s).statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:simplifiedZ(s)} The height zeta function is also given by \begin{align} Z(s)=\left(1-3^{-z}\right)^2\xi(z)^2R(z),\qquad z=\tfrac12(s_0+s_1+s_2), \end{align} where $\xi$ is the Dedekind zeta function of the cyclotomic field $\QQ(\sqrt{-3})$. The height zeta function has meromorphic continuation to the region $\{s \in (\CC^{\Sigma(1)})^{\Gamma} : \mathrm{Re}(s_0+s_1+s_2) > 1\}$. \end{lemma}

prop:leadingTerms.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:leadingTerms} The only pole of $Z_0(z)$ in the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(z)>1/2$ is a double pole at $z=1$. Its Laurent expansion there is \begin{equation}\label{eqn:Z0Laurent} Z_0(z)=\frac{\alpha}{9(z-1)^2} +\frac{2\alpha}{9}\left(\mu-\frac{\zeta'(2)}{\zeta(2)}+\beta +\frac38\log3\right)\frac{1}{z-1}+O(1), \end{equation} where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are as in \eqref{eqn:introConstants}. \end{proposition}

lemma:reducibles.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:reducibles} Let $d_n$ be the coefficients of $Z_0(z)=\sum_{n\geq1}d_n n^{-z}$. For $X\geq1$, \begin{equation}\label{eqn:weightedPolynomialCount} \sum_{\substack{f\in F\\H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)\leq\sqrt X}}1 =\frac12\sum_{n\leq X}d_n -\frac{\pi}{9\sqrt3}X+O(\sqrt X). \end{equation} \end{lemma}

lemma:generalHeightReduction.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:generalHeightReduction} For $s\in\ZZ$, define $\phi_s$ on $F_s$ by \[ \phi_s(f)(t)= \begin{cases} f(t+\tfrac{s}{3}),&s\equiv0\pmod3,\\ f(t+\tfrac{s-1}{3}),&s\equiv1\pmod3,\\ -f(-t+\tfrac{s+1}{3}),&s\equiv-1\pmod3. \end{cases} \] Then $\phi_s$ is a bijection from $F_s$ to $F_0$ if $3\mid s$, and from $F_s$ to $F_1$ if $3\nmid s$, and it preserves $n$. For $f\in F_s$, put $n=n(f)$. Then $n>0$, and \[ H(f)\leq H \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |s|\leq H\ \text{ and }\ n\leq s^2+3H^2. \] If $3\nmid s$, then $H_{\mathrm{tor}}(\phi_s(f))^2=n$. If $3\mid s$, then $\phi_s(f)=t^3-\frac n3t+c$ for some $c\in\ZZ$. \end{lemma}

lemma:traceZeroCoefficients.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:traceZeroCoefficients} Let $e$ be the exponent of $3$ in $N$, and write $N=3^eM$ with $3\nmid M$. Then \[ r(N)= \begin{cases} d_M,&e=0,\\ 3d_M+1,&N=3u^2\text{ for some }u\in\ZZ_{>0},\\ 3d_M,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \] \end{lemma}

eqn:generalTraceDecomposition.statement: \begin{align} \#\{f\in F_{\mathrm{mon}}:H(f)\leq H\} =\sum_{\substack{s\in\ZZ,\ |s|\leq H\\3\nmid s}} A_1(3H^2+s^2) +\sum_{\substack{s\in\ZZ,\ |s|\leq H\\3\mid s}} A_0\left(H^2+\frac{s^2}{3}\right). \label{eqn:generalTraceDecomposition} \end{align}

rem:translationClasses.statement: \begin{rem}\label{rem:translationClasses} We derive the count of translation classes by $H_{\mathrm{BS}}$ stated in the introduction. The invariant $I$ there is $n(f)$. Translating the roots by an integer $k$ changes the trace by $3k$ and preserves $n(f)$, so each translation class in $F_{\mathrm{mon}}$ has exactly one representative with trace in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The map $f(t)\mapsto-f(-t)$ negates the roots, so it matches the classes of trace $1$ with those of trace $-1$ and preserves $n(f)$. A trace-one polynomial $t^3-t^2+at+b$ has $n(f)=1-3a$, and $t^3-Nt+c$ has $n(f)=3N$. Hence the number $C(Y)$ of translation classes with $I\leq Y$ is \[ C(Y)=2A_1(Y)+A_0(Y/3). \] Substituting \eqref{eqn:A1asymptotic} and Proposition~\ref{prop:traceZeroAsymptotic}, and using that $Q$ is linear with leading coefficient $2\alpha/9$, gives \[ C(Y)=Y\left(\frac{11}{6}Q\left(\tfrac12\log Y\right) -\frac{19\alpha}{108}\log3-\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt3}\right) +O_\varepsilon(Y^{1/2+\varepsilon}). \] Since $f$ has three distinct real roots, $4I^3-J^2=27\operatorname{disc}(f)>0$, so $H_{\mathrm{BS}}(f)=I^3$. Setting $Y=H^{1/3}$ and substituting the formula for $Q$ from Corollary~\ref{cor:integralPointCount} gives the stated polynomial $P_{\mathrm{BS}}$ and error $O_\varepsilon(H^{1/6+\varepsilon})$. \end{rem}

thm:traceDistribution.statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:traceDistribution} Uniformly in $r$, $u_1$ and $u_2$, as $H\to\infty$, \[ N_r(H;u_1,u_2) =c_r\left(\int_{u_1}^{u_2}(3+u^2)\,du\right)H^3\log H+O(H^3), \qquad c_0=\frac{5\alpha}{81},\quad c_1=c_2=\frac{\alpha}{27}. \] Consequently, among the polynomials counted in Theorem~\ref{thm:generalMonicCount}, the proportions with trace congruent to $0$, $1$ and $2$ modulo $3$ tend to $5/11$, $3/11$ and $3/11$. Within each residue class, $\operatorname{Tr}(f)/H$ has limiting density $\frac{3}{20}(3+u^2)$ on $[-1,1]$. \end{theorem}

prop:surfaceIntegralCubic.statement: \begin{proposition}[Integral cubic model]\label{prop:surfaceIntegralCubic} The invariant cubics \[ A=e_1^3,\qquad B=e_1e_2,\qquad C=e_3,\qquad D=\delta \] identify $\SSS$ with the cubic hypersurface in $\PP^3_\ZZ$ defined by \begin{equation}\label{eqn:surfaceIntegralCubic} F(A,B,C,D):=B^3+AD^2-ABD+3ACD+A^2C-6ABC+9AC^2=0. \end{equation} The divisor $\DDD_0=\{e_1=0\}$ corresponds to the line $\{A=B=0\}$ in these coordinates. On the generic fiber, \begin{equation}\label{eqn:surfaceAnticanonical} 3D_0\sim-K,\qquad \mcO(3D_0)\cong\mcO(1),\qquad (-K)^2=3. \end{equation} In particular, this cubic embedding is anticanonical. \end{proposition}

prop:surfaceRationalForm.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:surfaceRationalForm} Over $\ZZ[1/6]$, $\SSS$ is isomorphic to the cubic hypersurface \begin{equation}\label{eqn:surfaceNormCubic} x_0(x_1^2+3x_2^2)=x_3^3 \end{equation} in $\PP_{\ZZ[1/6]}^3$. Its generic fiber $S$ is a del Pezzo surface of degree $3$ and geometric Picard rank $1$. Its three geometric singularities are of type $\mathbf A_2$: one is rational, and the other two are conjugate over $E=\QQ(\sqrt{-3})$. Over $E$, the coordinates $x_1'=x_1+\sqrt{-3}x_2$ and $x_2'=x_1-\sqrt{-3}x_2$ give the split toric cubic $x_0x_1'x_2'=x_3^3$. In these coordinates, $D_0=\{x_0=x_3=0\}$. \end{proposition}

prop:surfaceResolvedBoundary.statement: \begin{proposition}[Resolution and reduced boundary]\label{prop:surfaceResolvedBoundary} The surface $S$ admits a minimal resolution $\pi\colon X\to S$ over $\QQ$. Put $D_{\mathrm{red}}=(\pi^{-1}D_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Then $X$ is a weak del Pezzo surface of degree $3$, of geometric Picard rank $7$. The geometric components of $D_{\mathrm{red}}$ form a chain with self-intersections \begin{equation}\label{eqn:surfaceBoundaryChain} (-2)-(-2)-(-1)-(-2)-(-2). \end{equation} The divisor $L=-K_X-D_{\mathrm{red}}$ is nef and not numerically zero, but is not big. More precisely, \begin{equation}\label{eqn:surfaceLogIntersections} K_X\cdot D_{\mathrm{red}}=-1,\qquad D_{\mathrm{red}}^2=-1,\qquad L^2=0. \end{equation} \end{proposition}

prop:santensConstant.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:santensConstant} Let $\pi\colon X\to S$ be the minimal resolution, let $D\subset X$ be the reduced preimage of $D_0$, and put $U=X\setminus D$. The coordinate ring of the affine chart $\SSS\setminus\DDD_0$ pulls back to a finitely generated $\ZZ$-subalgebra \[ A:=\pi^*\Gamma(\SSS\setminus\DDD_0,\mathcal O) \subset\Gamma(U,\mathcal O). \] A point $P\in U(\QQ)$ is integral if $g(P)\in\ZZ$ for every $g\in A$. With this integral condition and the height $H(\pi(-),1)$, \cite[Theorem~8.7]{santens2023integral} gives \[ \#\{P\in(\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ):H(P,1)\leq B\} \sim cB^2\log B,\qquad c=\frac{2\alpha}{9}. \] \end{proposition}

lemma:normalityCriterion.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:normalityCriterion} Let $K/\QQ$ be a $C_3$-algebra and let $x\in K$ have characteristic polynomial $t^3-e_1t^2+e_2t-e_3$. Then $x$ is normal if and only if $e_1(e_1^2-3e_2)\neq0$. \end{lemma}

rem:heightCoefficients.statement: \begin{rem}\label{rem:heightCoefficients} Comparing Euler factors in \eqref{eqn:Z0factorization} gives the coefficients explicitly: $d_n=0$ if $3\mid n$, and if $3\nmid n$ then \[ d_n=\sum_{d\mid n}3^{\omega(d_1)}(-1)^{\Omega(d_2)}, \] where $d=d_1d_2$ with $d_1$ divisible only by primes $p\equiv1\pmod3$ and $d_2$ only by primes $q\equiv2\pmod3$. Equivalently, $d_n$ is the product of $3k+1$ over prime powers $p^k\parallel n$ with $p\equiv1\pmod3$ if every prime $q\equiv2\pmod3$ divides $n$ to an even power, and $d_n=0$ otherwise. \end{rem}

rem:localNonintegrability.statement: \begin{rem}\label{rem:localNonintegrability} The local Fourier transforms --- and therefore the entire Poisson summation argument --- must be computed \emph{before} restricting to the line in $\mathrm{Pic}^T(S) \otimes \CC$ spanned by the $T_E$-line bundle $\mathcal O(D_0)$ of interest since $x \mapsto H_v(x,-s,D_0)$ will not be integrable for any place $v \neq 3,\infty$ once either of $s_1$ or $s_2$ vanishes, no matter how large and positive $\mathrm{Re}(s_0)$ is. \end{rem}

rem:idealParametrization.statement: \begin{rem}\label{rem:idealParametrization} We prompted GPT-$6.1$ with the contents of an earlier version of this paper and asked it to identify the Dirichlet series in Theorem~\ref{thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula}. Using our Eisenstein parametrization (\S\ref{sec:quadraticParametrization}) it proved that \[ \sum_{P \in (\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ)} H(P)^{-s} = \sum_{\substack{0\ne J\subseteq\mcO_E\\ J+3\mcO_E=\mcO_E\\ \mathrm N J\text{ a cube}}} N^E_\QQ(J)^{-s/6} \] where $J \subset \mcO_E$ runs over integral nonzero ideals. It also found a result in the literature \cite{kuehleitnerNowak2004} that we previously missed. After translating the $C_3$-polynomial counting problem into an integral Diophantine problem on $S^{(-3)}$ (explained in the next section), K\"uhleitner--Nowak's~\cite[Corollary~2]{kuehleitnerNowak2004} can be used to obtain an shorter proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:integralPointCount} and Theorem~\ref{thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount} without using the toric method, and with an error term $O\bigl(H(\log H)^3(\log\log H)^2\bigr)$. We did not incorporate this argument as the toric approach has the merit of generalizing readily to other abelian groups where there is no analogue of \cite{kuehleitnerNowak2004}. \end{rem}

cite:topacogullari2021-thm1.5.source: B. Topacogullari, The fourth moment of individual Dirichlet L-functions on the critical line, Math. Z. 298 (2021) 577–624, arXiv:1909.11517 v1, Theorem 1.5 (source label 105). Cited in cubic_v2.tex, proof of lemma:heightCoefficientSum, as [Theorem~1.5]{topacogullari2021}.
cite:topacogullari2021-thm1.5.statement: Let ε > 0. Let K be a quadratic number field with discriminant D. Then we have, for T ≥ 1, ∫_1^T |ζ_K(1/2 + it)|² dt = ∫_1^T P_K(log t) dt + O(|D|^{2/3} T^{2/3+ε} + |D|^{5/4 − 3θ/2} T^{1/2+θ+ε}), where P_K is a quadratic polynomial, whose coefficients depend only on the field K, and where the implicit constant depends only on ε. [θ: any admissible bound towards Ramanujan–Petersson for exceptional spectral parameters, §3.1; θ = 7/64 is admissible by Kim–Sarnak.]

cite:santens2023integral-toric-counting.source: T. Santens, Manin’s conjecture for integral points on toric varieties, arXiv:2312.13914v2 (1 August 2025), Theorem 8.7 with Theorem 6.9, Lemmas 5.24, 3.9 and 3.24, and the measure conventions of Construction 4.25 and Lemma 4.27. Source inspected on 14 October 2026.
cite:santens2023integral-toric-counting.statement: Rank-two, permutation-Picard case on Res_{Q(sqrt(-3))/Q} Gm, for arbitrary smooth complete Galois fans, finite-type integral subalgebras, a canonical toric metric at the real place and toric metrics at the primes in Santens's class: finite local norms in p^Z (Definition 4.1), agreement with the real-place support function on the rays of U, and one integral support function at all but finitely many primes (Definition 4.14). Explicit fan/model/properness, unit, regular-function, integral-height-class, anticanonical and positivity conditions precede a finite bounded count and its asymptotic. The coefficient is defined by the dual-cone integral and actual normalized local integrals. This is a computational literature corollary; the current cubic count and its evaluated constant are not assumed. Corrected convergence factors, the rational Neron-Severi torus quotient and boundary-map signs are documented in the review.

cite:chandrasekharanNarasimhan1963-thm4.statement: For the actual quadratic field E=Q(sqrt(-3)), the normalized critical-line mean M(1/2,T)=(1/T) integral_1^T |zeta_E(1/2+it)|^2 dt is O((log T)^2) as T tends to infinity. The source gives M(sigma,T)=O(T^(n(1-sigma)-1) (log T)^n) for 1/n <= sigma <= 1-1/n; here n=2 and sigma=1/2. The Lean hypothesis is only the eventual upper bound with this normalization; all-T extension and the strip estimate are proved.

cite:kuehleitnerNowak2004-cor2.source: M. Kühleitner and W. G. Nowak, The average number of solutions of the Diophantine equation U^2 + V^2 = W^3 and related arithmetic functions, Acta Math. Hung. 104 (2004), 225–240; arXiv:math/0307221v1, Corollary 2 (PDF p.10), the residue formulation in the Theorem (PDF p.2), and equation (4.4). Authors’ preprint inspected on 2026-10-20.
cite:kuehleitnerNowak2004-cor2.statement: For each fixed quadratic number field K, let a_K(0)=0 and a_K(n) count actual integral ideals of absolute norm n^3 for n>=1. Its Dirichlet series D_K(s) converges absolutely for Re(s)>1. If F is analytic at 1 and agrees with (s-1)^2 D_K(s) on a real right-neighborhood of 1, then sum_{1<=n<=X} a_K(n) = F(1) X log X + (F′(1)-F(1)) X + O(sqrt(X) (log X)^3 (log log X)^2). This is Corollary 2 in its equivalent residue form; the constants may depend on K. The local-factor removal, original-point comparison, constant identification and height changes are not part of this hypothesis.

eqn:monicConceptualConstants.statement: \begin{equation}\label{eqn:monicConceptualConstants} \begin{aligned} C_{\mathrm{mon}} &=2\rho_E^2\mathcal E_{\mathrm{mon}}(1) \mathcal V_\infty(1),\\ D_{\mathrm{mon}} &=\frac{C_{\mathrm{mon}}}{2}\left( 2\gamma_E-1 +\frac{\mathcal E_{\mathrm{mon}}'(1)} {\mathcal E_{\mathrm{mon}}(1)} +\frac{\mathcal V_\infty'(1)} {\mathcal V_\infty(1)}\right) -\frac{\pi}{9\sqrt3}\mathcal V_\infty(1). \end{aligned} \end{equation}

lemma:heightCoefficientSum.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:heightCoefficientSum} For every $\varepsilon>0$, \begin{equation}\label{eqn:dSummatoryForGeneralTrace} \sum_{n\leq X}d_n =XQ\left(\tfrac12\log X\right) +O_\varepsilon(X^{1/2+\varepsilon}), \end{equation} where $Q$ is the polynomial of Corollary~\ref{cor:integralPointCount}. \end{lemma}
lemma:heightCoefficientSum.retired: 2026-11-02: folded into the proof of thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount; the current supporting statement is eqn:dSummatoryForGeneralTrace.

prop:surfaceAffineModel.statement: \begin{proposition}[Trace-one chart]\label{prop:surfaceAffineModel} In the coordinates $a=B/A$, $b=-C/A$, and $d=D/A$, the complement of the boundary is \begin{equation}\label{eqn:surfaceAffineModel} \SSS\setminus\DDD_0 =\operatorname{Spec}\frac{\ZZ[a,b,d]} {\bigl(d^2-(a+3b)d+a^3+6ab+9b^2-b\bigr)}. \end{equation} Here $a,b$ are the coefficients of $t^3-t^2+at+b$ used in the paper. A rational point of this chart is integral exactly when $a,b\in\ZZ$; the analogous criterion holds over every $\ZZ_p$. \end{proposition}

thm:allGaloisCounts.statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:allGaloisCounts} Let $\vartheta>1$ be the real root of $\vartheta^3-\vartheta^2-\vartheta-1=0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, as $H\to\infty$ through positive integers, \begin{align*} N_1(H)&=\frac{20\pi\sqrt3}{81}H^3+O(H^2),\\ N_{C_2}(H)&=\left(6+\vartheta-\frac{11}{3\vartheta} +4\log\vartheta\right)H^4\\ &\qquad+\left(1+\vartheta+\frac{2}{3\vartheta} +2\log\vartheta-\frac{20\pi\sqrt3}{27}\right)H^3 +O(H^2),\\ N_{C_3}(H)&=H^3P(\log H)+O_\varepsilon(H^{2+\varepsilon}),\\ N_{S_3}(H)&=8H^6+4H^5 -\left(2+\vartheta-\frac{11}{3\vartheta} +4\log\vartheta\right)H^4\\ &\qquad+H^3\left(5-\vartheta-\frac{2}{3\vartheta} -2\log\vartheta+\frac{40\pi\sqrt3}{81} -P(\log H)\right)\\ &\qquad+O_\varepsilon(H^{2+\varepsilon}). \end{align*} \end{theorem}
thm:allGaloisCounts.retired: Moved from Appendix C to the standalone Galois-group note on 2026-11-02. The statements and existing Lean proofs are retained; this label is no longer part of current-paper coverage.

rem:realHeightBounds.statement: \begin{rem}\label{rem:realHeightBounds} For arbitrary real $H\to\infty$, the formulas for $N_1(H)$ and $N_{C_3}(H)$ remain valid. Write $\{H\}=H-\lfloor H\rfloor$ and put \begin{align*} \mathcal R(H)={}&\left(6+\vartheta-\frac{11}{3\vartheta} +4\log\vartheta\right)H^4\\ &{}+(1-2\{H\})\left(1+\vartheta+\frac{2}{3\vartheta} +2\log\vartheta\right)H^3. \end{align*} Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$, \begin{align*} N_{C_2}(H)&=\mathcal R(H)-\frac{20\pi\sqrt3}{27}H^3+O(H^2),\\ N_{S_3}(H)&=\prod_{j=1}^3\bigl(2\lfloor H^j\rfloor+1\bigr) -\mathcal R(H)\\ &\qquad-H^3\left(P(\log H)-\frac{40\pi\sqrt3}{81}\right) +O_\varepsilon(H^{2+\varepsilon}). \end{align*} The function $\mathcal R(H)$ is the main term for cubics with a marked integral root. Its fractional-part term accounts for the boundary $|a_1|\leq H$, and the product counts the integer points in the full coefficient box. \end{rem}

lemma:splitCubicCount.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:splitCubicCount} The number of completely split monic integral cubics of height at most $H$, including those with repeated roots, is \[ N_1(H)=\frac{20\pi\sqrt3}{81}H^3+O(H^2). \] \end{lemma}

lemma:linearFactorSliceMoments.statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lemma:linearFactorSliceMoments} The function $g$ is even and twice continuously differentiable on $[-1,1]$. With $\vartheta$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:allGaloisCounts}, \begin{align*} \int_{-1}^1g(y)\,dy &=6+\vartheta-\frac{11}{3\vartheta}+4\log\vartheta,\\ g(1)&=1+\vartheta+\frac{2}{3\vartheta}+2\log\vartheta. \end{align*} \end{lemma}

prop:markedLinearFactorCount.statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:markedLinearFactorCount} Let $\mathcal R(H)$ be as in Remark~\ref{rem:realHeightBounds}. Counting each integral root once, the number of pairs $(f,r)$ with $f\in\ZZ[t]$ monic cubic, $H(f)\leq H$, and $f(r)=0$ is \[ \sum_{\substack{f\in\ZZ[t]\ \mathrm{monic}\\\deg f=3,\ H(f)\leq H}} \#\{r\in\ZZ:f(r)=0\} =\mathcal R(H)+O(H^2). \] \end{proposition}
